messages.text: Why is the inner / outer radius so different ?
I’ll check the model dimensions behind the two panels to explain the difference.

The two current models use **different detector envelopes**. The drawing preserves those actual dimensions.

| Boundary | Si–W¹ | LAr |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sampling front | 1700 mm | 2172.8 mm |
| Sampling back | 2223.2 mm | 2578.3 mm |
| Outer cover / cryostat | 2233.2 mm | 2830 mm |

¹ Si–W values are polygon **apothems**, measured at the sector centre.

The LAr prototype deliberately retained the ALLEGRO reference’s sampling radii, plane count and inclination. Its cryostat starts at **2100 mm**, with **72.8 mm** of walls, vacuum and bath before sampling, and **251.7 mm** behind sampling for bath/services and vessel walls. See [DES-032]([redacted]

So this compares the **current layouts and their gap topology**; their radial envelopes were never matched. The larger LAr radius is a retained prototype choice, rather than something established as necessary by this study.
